primitives.name: Power Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper proposes a power model to estimate tournament outcome probabilities based on past tournament data.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes win probability depends only on relative seeding ranks and follows a power law scaling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when seeding information is unavailable or unreliable.

layer2.mapping: GSI: The power model maps directly to a Bradley-Terry style logistic regression with a fixed scale parameter, enabling Bayesian inference about tournament outcomes through probabilistic bracket sampling.
layer2.telemetry: Observed frequency of higher seeds beating lower seeds serves as empirical telemetry for validating the power law assumption.

primitives.name: Bracket Pool Generation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Hence, rather than focusing on creating a single bracket to perform well, a challenge participant may wish to create a pool of brackets that likely contains at least one highscoring bracket.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B': 'Number of brackets in the pool (dimensionless)', 'b_i': 'Individual bracket (binary vector of game predictions)'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the goal is to maximize the probability of containing at least one high-scoring bracket, treating each bracket as an independent sample.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when bracket correlations due to shared generation methods reduce diversity below optimal levels.

layer2.mapping: GSE: Bracket pool generation implements a state-transition framework where each tournament round represents a branching decision node, and the pool evolves through sequential filtering and expansion based on conditional win probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Historical tournament progression data tracks the survival rate of initial bracket predictions, providing telemetry for assessing generation algorithm performance.

primitives.name: ESPN Scoring System

primitives.assumptions: Assumes point values increase exponentially with each round, giving disproportionate emphasis to late-stage predictions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the scoring weight becomes so skewed that early-round errors dominate overall performance variance.

layer2.mapping: GSI: The ESPN scoring system induces a non-uniform loss landscape, making it a conformal kernel for evaluating predictive models under asymmetric cost functions.
layer2.telemetry: Year-over-year variation in optimal bracket scores serves as telemetry for measuring tournament unpredictability.

primitives.verbatim_quote: However, the quantity and unpredictable nature of games suggest a single bracket will likely select some winning teams incorrectly even if created with insightful and sophisticated methods.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes independence among game outcomes and high individual error rates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when external factors introduce systematic biases that violate independence.
